title: Capacity drift stabilization and tenant fencing recovery playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-18 a dedicated-cluster capacity event caused elevated P95/P99 tail latencies and a short-lived spike in tenant evictions across two GPU pools. Impact included increased user-facing error rates for customers on Dedicated plans and multiple workload restarts. This ticket consolidates postmortem findings and tracks a prioritized recovery + prevention playbook addressing three correlated failure vectors: latent reservation mis-sizing (capacity drift), extended noisy-tenant bursts that exceeded fair-share expectations, and weak lateral isolation that allowed resource thrash to propagate.
action_items: ENG-86210-A1: Fix reservation decay math and eligibility window (owner: Liam Chen) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2481 - due 2026-03-17

ENG-86210-A2: Implement hard cap on continuous burst tokens per-tenant + reduce refill window from 60s->10s (owner: Priya Rao) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/burst-policy-tuning - due 2026-03-12

ENG-86210-A3: Add tenant soft-fencing path that throttles remaining connections when a tenant exceeds long-tail resource consumption (owner: Marcos Silva) - prototype in canary cluster - due 2026-03-20

ENG-86210-A4: Improve telemetry: per-tenant reservation utilization, burst-token consumption histograms, and eviction-event attribution fields (owner: SRE Observability team lead - K. Nguyen) - dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant_capacity/eviction-overview - due 2026-03-10
ENG-86210-A5: Create multi-tenant noisy workload test harness and run canonical replay of incident workload (owner: Test Infra - R. Alvarez) - results linked in supporting_artifacts - due 2026-03-15

ENG-86210-A6: Update Dedicated runbook with explicit mitigation steps (temporal reservation cap, tenant fencing, emergency rollback) and add a one-click automation to apply caps (owner: Oncall Tools - J. Park) - runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated_capacity - due 2026-03-08
ENG-86210-A7: Rollout plan: canary -> shard-by-shard -> global; include automated health gates for P95, eviction-rate, and errors (owner: Liam Chen) - start 2026-03-11
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows P95 latency reduced to <= 1.5x baseline during simulated noisy workload (baseline defined pre-incident)
Eviction rate in affected pools reduced to < 0.2 events/hour per pool for 72h
No customer-facing 5xx spikes during shard-by-shard rollout; automated rollback triggers tested
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant sustained burst > 30s and emits alert with tenant id and metric attribution
comments: 2026-02-20 09:14 — Liam Chen: Initial triage: observed unexpected reservation decay on pool gpu-dedicated-6. Correlated with one tenant generating repeated long-running fanout requests. Created temporary reservation cap and disabled long-refill bursts; immediate tail latency improved ~42%

Hypotheses: (1) reservation decay uses wall-clock window that double-counts overlapping windows, (2) burst token controller lacks sliding-window enforcement, allowing effective unlimited sustained bursts for sustained high concurrency
